paragraphs.title: A Call to Give the Lord Glory and Strength

easy.explanation: Verse 1 begins, “Give unto the LORD, O ye mighty.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalm call upon to give glory and strength to the LORD?

answers: The glory due unto his name
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name.”
easy.q: What are they told to give unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse commands, “worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness.”
easy.q: What are they commanded to do before the LORD?

medium.explanation: The verses mention glory, strength, the glory due to God’s name, and holiness.
medium.q: Which qualities are emphasized in verses 1–2?

medium.explanation: The people are told to give glory and worship the LORD.
medium.q: How is recognition of the LORD’s glory expressed in this passage?

answers: Worship marked by holiness and reverence
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the reverent and holy manner in which the LORD is worshiped.
medium.q: What does “the beauty of holiness” describe?

answers: Even the powerful must acknowledge the LORD’s greatness
Only the weak must worship the LORD
The passage is mainly about forests
challenge.explanation: The mighty are called to give the LORD glory and strength, showing that all people must honor Him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the address “O ye mighty”?

answers: Worship is a practical expression of giving him honor
challenge.explanation: The command to give glory is followed by the command to worship, linking honor with action.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between giving glory and worshiping the LORD?

challenge.explanation: These words create an atmosphere of deep respect, power, and sacredness.
challenge.q: What atmosphere is created by the words “glory,” “strength,” and “holiness”?

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Voice in Power and Majesty

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “The voice of the LORD is upon the waters.”
easy.q: Where is the voice of the LORD heard?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the God of glory thundereth.”
easy.q: What does the God of glory do?

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “The voice of the LORD is powerful” and “is full of majesty.”
easy.q: How is the LORD’s voice described in verse 4?

answers: The thunder displays his power and glory
medium.explanation: The thunder presents the voice of the glorious God as mighty and impressive.
medium.q: How does the thunder relate to the description of God as the God of glory?

answers: From the voice over the waters to its power and majesty
From the temple to the wilderness
From fire to the birth of animals
medium.explanation: The passage first places the voice over the waters, then describes its character as powerful and majestic.
medium.q: How does the description develop in verses 3–4?

answers: Makes a loud sound like thunder
medium.explanation: “Thundereth” means that the God of glory speaks with the sound and force of thunder.
medium.q: What does “thundereth” mean in this context?

answers: His strength is joined with splendor and greatness
His power is opposed to his majesty
His voice is only a natural sound
challenge.explanation: The two descriptions together show both the force and the royal splendor of the LORD.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by describing the LORD’s voice as both powerful and majestic?

answers: The vast setting increases the sense of greatness
challenge.explanation: The broad expanse of many waters makes the voice seem even more immense and powerful.
challenge.q: Why do “many waters” strengthen the image of the LORD’s voice?

answers: The voice is first located and then described by its qualities
The passage moves from peace to war
The passage moves from the temple to the wilderness
challenge.explanation: Verse 3 describes where the voice is heard, while verse 4 explains that it is powerful and majestic.
challenge.q: What movement of thought occurs between verses 3 and 4?

paragraphs.title: The Voice That Shakes the World and Gives Life

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “The voice of the LORD breaketh the cedars.”
easy.q: What does the voice of the LORD do to the cedars?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “The voice of the LORD divideth the flames of fire.”
easy.q: What does the voice of the LORD divide?

answers: Every one speaks of his glory
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “in his temple doth every one speak of his glory.”
easy.q: What happens in the LORD’s temple?

answers: Breaking cedars, shaking the wilderness, dividing fire, and causing hinds to calve
Bringing gentle rain and quiet growth
medium.explanation: The passage describes the voice breaking cedars, dividing fire, shaking the wilderness, and causing hinds to calve.
medium.q: Which effects of the LORD’s voice are described in verses 5–9?

answers: The voice shakes and breaks nature, yet also causes hinds to give birth
The voice only creates and never shakes anything
medium.explanation: The voice brings violent natural effects but also causes the hinds to calve.
medium.q: How does the passage combine destruction with life?

answers: Causes the female deer to give birth
medium.explanation: To calve means to give birth, so the verse presents the LORD’s voice as bringing forth life.
medium.q: What does “maketh the hinds to calve” mean?

answers: Nature is shaken, while the temple is filled with glory
Nature is silent, while the temple is destroyed
Both nature and the temple are described as empty
challenge.explanation: The wilderness and forests are shaken, but in the temple everyone speaks of the LORD’s glory.
challenge.q: What contrast is presented between nature and the temple?

answers: Its power includes judgment, transformation, and the creation of life
Its power has only one effect
challenge.explanation: The different effects show that the LORD’s voice has wide power over destruction, change, and life.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the voice both breaks and gives birth?

answers: It shows that the voice affects both the environment and living creatures
It limits the voice to the temple
It focuses only on the beauty of trees
challenge.explanation: The voice shakes the forests and causes the hinds to give birth, affecting both nature and animals.
challenge.q: How does the mention of the forests and hinds broaden the description of the voice?

paragraphs.title: The Eternal King Who Blesses with Peace

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “The LORD sitteth upon the flood.”
easy.q: Where does the LORD sit according to verse 10?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the LORD sitteth King for ever.”
easy.q: How long does the LORD sit as King?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “The LORD will give strength unto his people.”
easy.q: What does the LORD give to his people?

answers: The LORD reigns forever, gives strength, and blesses with peace
The LORD shakes the wilderness and breaks cedars
The people give the LORD water and fire
medium.explanation: The passage moves from the LORD’s eternal kingship to his gifts of strength and peace.
medium.q: What is the main sequence in verses 10–11?

answers: He gives his people both power and peaceful well-being
Peace is described as another storm
medium.explanation: The final verse joins two blessings: strength for the people and peace from the LORD.
medium.q: How are strength and peace related in the LORD’s blessing?

answers: A guardian of the forest only
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the LORD as a ruler whose kingship never ends.

answers: As the eternal King who remains sovereign over it
As one who flees from it
As one who disappears beneath it
challenge.explanation: The LORD sits upon the flood and remains King forever, showing that the flood does not overcome him.
challenge.q: How does verse 10 portray the LORD in relation to the flood?

answers: The LORD’s rule brings his people from turmoil toward strength and peace
Peace is portrayed as a stronger flood
challenge.explanation: The psalm moves from overwhelming waters to the LORD’s blessing of strength and peace.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from the flood to peace?

answers: It connects the LORD’s power with his blessing of his people
It focuses only on the cedars of Lebanon
It rejects the earlier emphasis on glory
challenge.explanation: The final verse joins the LORD’s great power with his gracious gifts of strength and peace.
challenge.q: How does verse 11 summarize the main ideas of the psalm?
